constructions.title: Danish livestock as official counts, throughput, and nitrogen derived from them

pigs_standing.is: Pigs standing in Denmark at one moment, Statistics Denmark table `SVIN`, type `D29`, for the quarter named in `pigs_standing_period`; the table reports thousands and the script multiplies up.

sows_standing.is: Sows standing, table `SVIN`, type `D181`, same quarter, multiplied up from thousands.

pigs_through_per_year.is: Pigs slaughtered or exported live in the year named in `pigs_through_period`, table `ANI5`; the throughput, not the stock. Animals that died on the farm are not in it.

pig_meat_million_kg_per_year.is: Pig meat production in the same year, table `ANI5`, kept in the table's own unit of million kg.

cattle_standing.is: Cattle standing, whole country, table `KVAEG5`, type `D17`, for the quarter in `cattle_period`.

people.is: People living in Denmark, table `FOLK1A`, for the quarter in `people_period`.

manure_n_kt_per_year.is: A stated manure-and-sludge nitrogen figure per hectare from the field balance in DCE `SR120` times the current agricultural area from `data/derived/cropland.json`, in kt.

human_sewage_n_kt_per_year.*.is: People times a stated per-person sewage nitrogen convention, at both ends of the stated range, in kt.

manure_over_human.is: Manure nitrogen divided by human sewage nitrogen at the low end of the per-person range.

pig_years_per_pig_stated.is: The life of a Danish slaughter pig in years, written into the script as a stated figure.

liveborn_per_sow_year_stated.*.is: A stated range of piglets born alive per sow-year; the script carries both ends.

died_before_slaughter_share_stated.*.is: A stated range for the share of liveborn pigs that never reach slaughter or export.

born_per_year_from_sows.*.is: Sows standing times the stated liveborn range: pigs born in a year, by the sow route.

born_per_year_from_throughput.*.is: The throughput grossed up by the stated share that dies first: pigs born in a year, by the throughput route.

died_before_slaughter_per_year.*.is: The throughput-route births minus the throughput: pigs that died before slaughter or export, at both ends of the stated share.

constructions.what: Fetches the official Danish counts of pigs, sows, cattle and people and the annual pig throughput, and derives manure and sewage nitrogen and the pigs that die before slaughter.
constructions.model: Each count is the last value of a Statistics Denmark API query for a named table and period (in the code `one()`). Manure nitrogen is $N_{ha} \times A$ with $N_{ha}$ the stated field-balance figure and $A$ the agricultural area; sewage nitrogen is people times a stated per-person figure. Births are estimated two ways: sows times liveborn per sow-year, and throughput divided by one minus the share that dies first; deaths are the second minus the throughput.
assumptions: The quarter and year named in the query are the current ones; they are written into the script.
The field-balance manure figure per hectare still applies to the current agricultural area.
The stated liveborn and mortality ranges describe the current Danish herd.

justified.text: The counts are the national statistics office's own tables, fetched live from its API.
The two birth routes are independent, and the script prints both so a disagreement would be visible.

gaps: The liveborn range, the mortality share and the pig lifetime are stated in the script without a pinned source.
The manure figure per hectare is from an older field balance and is not re-derived for the current year.
No open series of on-farm deaths exists that this project has found, so the deaths are arithmetic on stated ranges, not a count.
void_if: Statistics Denmark redefines a table type code or changes a table's unit
the field balance behind the manure figure is superseded
constructions.licenses: The size of the Danish herd relative to its human population, the difference between stock and throughput, and the order of magnitude of manure nitrogen against sewage nitrogen.
constructions.not_licensed: A measured count of pigs that died on farms; the nitrogen that reaches any water.

constructions.title: The rain stream and the foul stream on Amager, as rates

rain_record.years.is: Distinct calendar years with at least one hourly precipitation value in the fetched `ERA5` files under `data/raw/weather/`.

rain_record.hours.is: Hourly precipitation values in those files, missing values skipped.

rain_record.mean_annual_mm.is: Total hourly precipitation over the record divided by the number of years. `ERA5` is a reanalysis: the output of a weather model constrained by observations, at a grid cell far coarser than a city.

rain_record.wet_hours_per_year.is: Hours with precipitation above zero, per year of record.

rain_record.hours_per_year_at_or_above_m.is: Hours at or above each stated threshold, per year of record.

rain_record.median_wet_hour_mm.is: The median of the hours with precipitation above zero.

rain_record.max_hour_mm.is: The largest hourly value in the record. A grid-cell mean cannot reproduce a cloudburst, so this is far below what a street experiences.

*.design_intensity_mm_h_stated.is: The design rain intensity, a convention written into `scripts/programme.py` as `RAIN_MM_H`.

*.runoff_coefficient_stated.is: The share of rain on paved surface that runs off, a design convention written into `scripts/programme.py` as `RUNOFF_C`.

*.flow_m3_s.design_hour.is: Amager's combined-sewered impervious area times the design intensity times the runoff coefficient, in cubic metres per second.

*.flow_m3_s.median_wet_hour.is: The same area times the median wet-hour precipitation times the runoff coefficient.

foul_stated.dwf_l_per_person_day.is: Dry-weather sewage per person per day, a design convention.

foul_stated.morning_peak_factor.is: The ratio of the morning peak to the mean dry-weather flow, a design convention.

foul_stated.morning_peak_m3_s_per_1000_p.is: The dry-weather flow of a thousand people times the peak factor.

foul_stated.people_matched_per_imperviou.is: How many people's morning peak one impervious hectare matches in the design hour.

foul_stated.people_matched_by_amager_in_.is: How many people's morning peak Amager's impervious area matches in the design hour.

foul_stated.people_matched_by_amager_at_.is: The same at the median wet hour.

ponds.*.grain_um.is: The grain diameters the script chooses to size ponds for, in micrometres.

ponds.*.settling_m_per_h.is: Stokes terminal velocity of a quartz-density grain in still water, from the viscosity and densities stated in the script.

ponds.*.area_ha_at_design_hour.is: The pond area whose surface loading equals the settling velocity when the design-hour flow arrives at once.

ponds.*.area_ha_if_fed_steadily.is: The pond area that suffices when the year's runoff is fed at a steady rate.

sediment.tss_mg_per_l_stated.is: A suspended-solids concentration for urban stormwater, chosen inside the range the script's comment cites.

sediment.capture_fraction_stated.is: The share of arriving solids a pond keeps, taken as the low end of the pond range PROGRAMME.md quotes.

sediment.solids_caught_t_per_year.is: Annual runoff volume times the stated concentration times the stated capture, in tonnes.

sediment.solids_caught_m3_per_year.is: The caught tonnage divided by a stated bulk density.

sediment.t_per_impervious_ha_per_year.is: Caught tonnage per impervious hectare on Amager.

sediment.m3_per_impervious_ha_per_year.is: Caught volume per impervious hectare on Amager.

constructions.what: Turns the hourly rain record over Copenhagen and Amager's combined-sewered impervious area into flow rates, compares them with the foul stream as people-equivalents, sizes settling ponds for chosen grains, and estimates the solids a pond would catch.
constructions.model: Flow is $Q = A \cdot i \cdot C / 3600$ with $A$ in square metres, $i$ in metres per hour and $C$ the runoff coefficient (in the code `flow()`). Settling is Stokes, $v = (\rho_s - \rho_w) g d^2 / (18 \mu)$ (in the code `settling_m_per_h()`); the peak-fed pond area is the design-hour volume over $v$, the steady-fed area is annual runoff over $v$ times the hours in a year. Solids caught are runoff volume times concentration times capture.
assumptions: A grid-cell reanalysis stands for the rain over Amager's streets.
Ponds settle as still water, so the areas are floors.
Amager's combined-sewered impervious area is split from the mainland by the hand-drawn polygon in `scripts/programme.py`.

justified.text: Every formula and every stated convention is written out in the script, and the stated values are carried into the output under names ending in `_stated`.
The rain record is the fetched hourly series, not a design storm.

gaps: The runoff coefficient, dry-weather flow, peak factor, concentration, capture fraction and bulk density are conventions without pinned sources.
The capture fraction is taken from the pond literature quoted on PROGRAMME.md, whose sources are not pinned; the page and this file lean on each other there.
A reanalysis grid cell smooths away the short intense rain that drives overflows, so the rain statistics understate the extremes.
void_if: the weather files under `data/raw/weather/` are replaced by a different point or product
the Amager polygon or the catchment layer changes
constructions.licenses: The rain stream against the foul stream as rates, the pond areas a settling filter needs as floors, and the order of magnitude of what a pond would catch.
constructions.not_licensed: A cloudburst frequency for any street; a measured pond performance; a sediment tonnage anyone has weighed.

constructions.title: How much of the modelled flood path has a planned route near it

flood_path_km2.is: The area of flooded cells in the recovered flood model sheets on the common grid of `scripts/floodgap.py`, harbour and lakes removed, in km².

near_buried_conveyance_pct.is: Flooded cells within `NEAR_M` of a planned cloudburst pipe, as a percentage of all flooded cells.

near_anything_pct.is: Flooded cells within `NEAR_M` of a planned surface route, a pipe or a basin, as a percentage of all flooded cells.

no_surface_route_pct.is: Flooded cells with no planned surface route within `NEAR_M`, as a percentage of all flooded cells.

constructions.what: Rasterises the recovered flood model and the cloudburst plan, split into surface routes and pipes, and measures how much of the flood path each comes near.
constructions.model: Distance transforms of the rasterised plan layers; a flooded cell is near a layer when its distance is at most `NEAR_M`. Each share is near cells over all flooded cells on the same grid (in the code `main()`).
assumptions: The recovered sheets are placed where the georeferencing says.
The plan layers are complete for the cloudburst plan.

justified.text: Numerator and denominator are counted on the same grid from the same flooded mask.

gaps: The sheets are tied to the ground with errors comparable to the proximity distance, so a cell's nearness can move with a placement.
The flood extent is a model output, not an observation of flooding.
void_if: a sheet is re-registered or withdrawn
constructions.licenses: How far the cloudburst plan's surface routes reach the modelled flood paths, against its pipes.
constructions.not_licensed: Where water will flow in a real event; that a planned route discharges anywhere in particular.

constructions.title: Modelled flooding scored against local terrain, per sheet

sheets.*.windows.*.flooded_below_local_p.is: Of the sampled flooded pixels on land, the percentage whose elevation is below the median terrain of the block of that window size around them.

sheets.*.windows.*.background_below_loca.is: The same for the background sample, taken along streets where the road extract is present and uniformly otherwise.

sheets.*.windows.*.lift_pct_points.is: The flooded percentage minus the background percentage, in percentage points.

constructions.what: Fetches the national elevation model for each flood sheet and asks whether modelled flooding sits below its own neighbourhood more often than street ground does.
constructions.model: For each window the terrain anomaly is elevation minus the block median (in the code `anomaly()`); flooded and background samples are scored below zero or not, land only, and the shares compared (in the code `one_sheet()`).
assumptions: The sheet's georeferencing is good enough for the window size used.
Street points are a fair background for flooding that lies mostly on streets.

justified.text: The elevation model is fetched live from the national service, and each sheet is scored against its own background.
The background is taken along streets so that interpolated ground under buildings does not stand in for street ground.

gaps: The samples are random with fixed seeds; the sampling error is not reported.
Positional error in the sheets is comparable to the smallest window.
void_if: the national elevation model is revised
constructions.licenses: Whether modelled flooding favours locally low ground, sheet by sheet.
constructions.not_licensed: Where water collects in a real event; why the model placed flooding where it did.

constructions.title: How well each recovered flood sheet is tied to the ground

*.m_per_px_from_scalebar.is: Metres per pixel of the rendered sheet, read from the sheet's own printed scale bar.

*.spread_m.is: For a sheet registered automatically: the largest distance between the positions found by the detector variants that agreed. It is conditioned on agreement, so it is small by construction.

*.standard_error_m.is: For a sheet placed from resident-reported control points: a positional standard error written into the file with the placement. No script in the repository computes it.

*.control_points.is: For a sheet placed by hand: the control points a resident reported on a web map and the placement used.

constructions.what: Records, per flood sheet, how it was placed and how far its placement can be trusted: the scale-bar resolution, the detector spread for automatic sheets, and the control points and standard error for assisted ones.
constructions.model: Automatic sheets are placed by ensemble water cross-correlation in `scripts/floodmaps.py`, which writes the agreeing spread and the scale-bar resolution. Assisted sheets were placed from control points; their standard errors entered the file with the placement commits.
assumptions: The printed scale bar is right.
The control points were read off the web map correctly.

justified.text: The automatic registration and its spread are computed in the script, with the acceptance thresholds explained beside the code.

gaps: No script in the repository writes `standard_error_m`; it arrived with the placement commits and cannot be recomputed here.
The agreeing spread measures agreement between detectors, not error against the ground.
void_if: a sheet is re-registered, which has already happened once
constructions.licenses: The order of magnitude of positional error per sheet, and which sheets were placed automatically.
constructions.not_licensed: A calibrated positional error for any sheet.

constructions.title: The separated architecture on the city's own sewer layer

street_m.amager.is: Road centreline length inside the combined-sewered catchments on Amager, from the untagged road extract. Paths and service roads are included, so it is an upper bound.

structures.rist.total.is: Gully gratings in the city's structure register.

structures.broend.total.is: Wells and chambers in the city's structure register.

structures.*.type_field_empty_pct.is: Register entries whose type column is empty, as a percentage of all entries in the same layer.

catchments.*.ri.is: Gully gratings whose point falls inside the catchment polygon.

catchments.*.br.is: Wells and chambers whose point falls inside the catchment polygon.

plan_pipe_ends.n.is: Planned cloudburst pipe segments with an end point in the plan layer.

plan_pipe_ends.median_m.is: The median, over segments, of the distance from the nearer end to the coast or the harbour.

plan_pipe_ends.within_50m.is: Segments whose nearer end lies within the distance in the field name of the coast or the harbour.

polder.ha.is: The Vestamager polder's area, written into `scripts/programme.py` as `VESTAMAGER_HA`; the outline beside it is schematic.

totals.combined.ha.is: The municipal layer's impervious area, summed over the catchments classed combined.

constructions.what: Classifies the city's sewer catchments, counts the drainage structures in them, measures the street a rain line would follow, and tests where planned cloudburst pipes end.
constructions.model: Point-in-polygon counts on a coarse spatial index for structures and street segments (in the code `structures()` and `street_metres()`); nearest-point distances to coast and harbour for pipe ends (in the code `plan_pipe_ends()`); sums of the layer's own attributes for totals.
assumptions: The municipal sewer-catchment layer's impervious area and class are right.
A structure belongs to the catchment its point falls in.

justified.text: The counts are taken from the city's own registers, and the script says which fields are empty rather than filling them.
The street length is labelled an upper bound in the output itself.

gaps: The road extract carries no tags, so street length cannot be restricted to carriageway.
The pipe-end test is evidence about a segmented layer, not about where any route discharges.
The polder area is a stated round figure, not measured from a boundary.
void_if: the municipal catchment layer or the structure register is refetched with different content
the cloudburst plan layer is revised
constructions.licenses: The scale of a separation retrofit in structures and in street length, and that the pipe layer is segmented.
constructions.not_licensed: The cost of any street; where a planned pipe discharges; the polder's surveyed extent.

constructions.title: Rain-conditioned outfalls and their basin volume, per coastal water body

areas.*.rbu.is: Points of the national rain-conditioned outfall register `punkt_rbu_udl` that `scripts/areas.py` assigns to the water body.

areas.*.vol.is: The registered basin volume `vol_sb` summed over those points, in m³. Registered, so a floor: a basin nobody entered is not here.

constructions.what: Carries each water body's outfall count and registered basin volume from the areas analysis into the published per-area file.
constructions.model: `scripts/areas.py` assigns register points to water bodies and sums `vol_sb`; `scripts/areamap.py` copies the count and the sum into the slim per-area record.
assumptions: The assignment of an outfall to the water body it discharges to is right.

justified.text: Both numbers are read straight from the national register, counted and summed without adjustment.

gaps: The register's volume field is empty for many points, so the sum understates the storage that exists.
void_if: the register is refetched with different content
the assignment of points to water bodies changes
constructions.licenses: A floor on the registered storage draining to a water body, and how many registered outfalls reach it.
constructions.not_licensed: The storage that actually exists; how much water overflows.

constructions.title: Karlstrup Kalkgrav's registered area, depth and pumping, as transcribed

karlstrup_kalkgrav.water_body.area_km2.is: The lake's area as registered in the water-plan data for `DKLAKE812`, transcribed by hand from the page the file links.

karlstrup_kalkgrav.physical_setting.dept.is: The lake's depth, transcribed by hand; the file names no source for it.

karlstrup_kalkgrav.physical_setting.pump.is: The volume the pump station removes to the bay each year, transcribed by hand; the file names no source for it.

constructions.what: Holds the physical facts about Karlstrup Kalkgrav that PROGRAMME.md weighs against using it as a receiving water.
constructions.model: Manual transcription into `data/manual/monitoring.json`; nothing is computed.
assumptions: The transcriptions are faithful to their sources.

justified.text: The area comes with a link to the water-plan record it was read from.

gaps: None of the sources is pinned, so none of the values can be checked against a stored copy.
The depth and the pumped volume have no named source in the file at all.
void_if: the water-plan register revises the lake's area
constructions.licenses: That the lake is small, deep and already pumped to the bay, as grounds for the page's argument against using it.
constructions.not_licensed: Any statement of the lake's current condition.

constructions.title: Counts and sums PROGRAMME.md computes for itself

amager_split.amager_ha.is: Impervious area of the combined-sewered catchments in the municipal layer whose vertex mean falls inside the hand-drawn Amager polygon, summed, in hectares.

amager_split.mainland_ha.is: The same for the combined-sewered catchments outside it.

rbu_register.points.is: Features in the national rain-conditioned outfall register `punkt_rbu_udl`.

rbu_register.with_volume.is: Of those, the features with a registered basin volume `vol_sb` above zero.

rbu_register.top_one_pct_n.is: The largest one per cent of the features with a volume, by volume, rounded down and at least one.

rbu_register.top_one_pct_share_pct.is: Their summed volume as a percentage of the summed volume of all features with a volume.

combined_catchments.planned_to_separate.is: Of those, the ones whose city plan class takes them out of the combined system: separate, three-pipe, foul only, or part separate.

flood_sheets.total.is: Sheets with a provenance entry in `data/derived/terraincheck.json`.

flood_sheets.automatic.is: Of those, the sheets whose placement method begins `autoref`.

flood_sheets.assisted.is: Of those, the sheets whose placement method begins `assisted`.

rivermap_corridors.is: Entries in the corridor list of `data/derived/rivermap.json`: the largest candidates the map draws, not every candidate.

constructions.what: Counts the overflow register's tail, the sheets by placement method, the combined catchments planned for separation and the corridor list, and splits the combined-sewered area by island. The triage and register counts the page prints are read from `data/derived/triage.json`, not computed here.
constructions.model: Feature counts with the rules stated per field (in the code `facts()`); the top share is $\sum_{i \le k} v_i / \sum_i v_i$ over volumes sorted descending, with $k$ the rounded-down one per cent; the island split is a point-in-polygon test on each catchment's vertex mean (in the code `amager_split()`).
assumptions: A catchment's vertex mean falls on the island the catchment is on.
A sheet's placement method is recorded in its provenance entry with the prefix the counts test for.

justified.text: Every count is taken from the file named in its description, with the rule written beside the code.

gaps: The Amager polygon is traced by hand; a catchment straddling its edge goes wholly to one side.
The top share uses only features with a registered volume; features with an empty volume field are outside both numerator and denominator.
void_if: the overflow register or the catchment layer is refetched with different content
a flood sheet's placement method is renamed
constructions.licenses: The counts and shares PROGRAMME.md prints about its own sources.
constructions.not_licensed: The storage that actually exists behind features with an empty volume field; the load any structure discharges.

constructions.title: Tallies over the collected public statements

n_speakers.is: Distinct speaker strings among them; a person described in different words is counted once per description.

n_sources.is: Distinct host names among the statements' source addresses.

camps.*.is: Statements whose id prefix assigns them to the camp named in the key, by the prefix table in the script; the longest matching prefix wins.

classes.*.is: Statements carrying the claim class named in the key, as the collection assigned it at capture.

flags.*.is: Statements carrying the flag named in the key, as the collection assigned it at capture.

flag_camps.*.*.is: Statements carrying the flag in the first key and assigned to the camp in the second.

domains.*.n.is: Statements whose source address has the host name in the same entry.

n_share.is: Statements whose quotation states the agricultural nitrogen share, or the diffuse total it is carved out of, matched by the pattern `SHARE_RX` in the script.

n_share_flagged.is: Of those, the ones the collection flags as stating a modelled quantity as measured.

constructions.what: Counts the collected public statements by camp, claim class, flag, publisher and date, for the page that prints them.
constructions.model: Counters over the statement list (in the code `analyse()`); the camp of a statement is the camp of the longest id prefix in `CAMPS` that it starts with.
assumptions: The claim classes and flags assigned at capture are the ones to count; the script does not reclassify.
An id prefix identifies the speaker's position in the process.

justified.text: Every count is a counter over the collection's own fields, and an id with no camp stops the build rather than being dropped.

gaps: The classes and flags are one collector's judgement at capture time; nobody has re-read the statements against them.
The collection is skewed toward the side that published press releases, so every count describes the record, not the debate.
void_if: statements are added to or removed from the collection
a flag or class is reassigned
constructions.licenses: How the collected record is composed: who is in it, how often, and with which classes and flags.
constructions.not_licensed: How the public debate as a whole was composed; that any statement is right or wrong.
